title: Experiment: the same rejection contract holds under runtime MDX compilation
summary: The identical remark plugin was run through `@mdx-js/mdx`'s `compile` + `run` in a Node process rather than a bundler, against the same six documents, rendering with `renderToStaticMarkup`. accept: compiled; reject-import: refused @ 1:1; reject-expression: refused @ 3:8; reject-attr-expression: refused @ 3:10; reject-spread: refused @ 3:10; reject-unmapped: refused @ 3:1. All six matched the build-time outcomes, and every refusal carried a position and the source path.

omissions.reason: Compilation and rendering were exercised directly, not inside a Next.js Server Component behind DEC-0019's `connection()` boundary. Composing the two is the next step and has not been run.
Timing was not collected. Whether compiling a stage document per request is acceptable at the sizes this project produces is unmeasured.

notes: ⚠️ THIS BECAME LOAD-BEARING ONLY BECAUSE OF THE FRESHNESS FINDING. If file-routed MDX had reflected edits, runtime compilation would never have been needed and this would be a curiosity. As it stands the requirements force runtime compilation, runtime compilation of author-controlled MDX is the exact shape of CVE-2026-0969, and this is the measurement that says the plugin still refuses there.
